entities.summary: Emperor Zhi of Han was a significant ruler of the Chinese Han dynasty, reigning from 146 AD to 25 July 146 AD. His reign was dominated by Liang Ji, the brother of Empress Dowager Liang, who eventually poisoned the young emperor. This event had a profound impact on the Eastern Han dynasty, leading to a period of instability and power struggles. Emperor Zhi's legacy is also marked by his attempts to reform the imperial examination system, but these efforts were ultimately unsuccessful. The emperor's death marked the beginning of a new era of instability in China, with the dynasty eventually falling to the warlords. The legacy of Emperor Zhi of Han can be seen in the many historical records that detail his reign and its significance. One of the most striking aspects of his reign was the extensive use of paper money, which was introduced during his rule. This innovative financial tool had far-reaching consequences for the economy and society of China, and its impact can still be felt today. As the 10th emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty, Emperor Zhi of Han played a crucial role in shaping the course of Chinese history. His life and reign offer a fascinating glimpse into the complexities and challenges of ruling a vast and diverse empire.
